overall_summary: Analysis of 47 unique shorts reveals a massive performance divergence across content pillars. High-stakes immersive 'What If You Fell Into...' and extreme cosmic anomaly concepts consistently dominate the channel, capturing 800-1,000+ views and 15-38 likes with active comment engagement. In contrast, psychology/brain trivia ('fake memories', 'songs stuck in head') and repeated re-uploads severely underperform (5-70 views, 0-1 likes). Furthermore, 19-21 second runtimes substantially outperform shorter 12-16 second videos by allowing enough narrative pacing to build curiosity and deliver a satisfying punchline.

winning_patterns.pattern: Second-Person 'What If You Fell Into...' Survival Hooks
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' achieved 1,029 views, 38 likes, and 2 comments; 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' gained 972 views and 18 likes; 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' hit 823 views and 15 likes.
winning_patterns.action: Standardize the second-person immersive survival framing ('What If You Fell Into / Drifted Near...') to turn passive astronomy facts into high-retention cinematic micro-dramas.

winning_patterns.pattern: Extreme Cosmic & Planetary Extremes (Darkest, Coldest, Most Violent)
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' reached 1,029 views (36 likes, 2 comments), 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' hit 981 views (21 likes), and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' gained 723 views (25 likes).
winning_patterns.action: Focus topic selection on specific, named astronomical horrors and physics anomalies that defy everyday logic, highlighting sensory extremes (absolute darkness, supersonic gemstones, temporal paradoxes).

winning_patterns.evidence: Top 5 performers all sit precisely between 19s and 21s duration, while sub-16s videos averaged under 150 views and frequently logged 0 comments.
winning_patterns.action: Target scripts between 19 and 21 seconds (approximately 50-55 spoken words) to secure a 3-act micro-arc: visceral hook, scientific reality, mind-bending conclusion.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' logged only 5, 10, and 53 views across three separate uploads; 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' got 38 views; 'Songs Stuck in Your Head' peaked at 17-71 views.
weak_patterns.action: Halt standalone, textbook psychology trivia unless reframed through high-stakes survival or dark evolutionary mystery.

weak_patterns.evidence: Duplicate concepts ('Why Space Is Completely Silent' tested three times: 34, 87, 220 views; 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' repeated with flat engagement).
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict deduplication; do not re-upload identical or near-identical concepts without a complete overhaul of visual direction and hook angle.
